why: Shorter, three questions, ties to the student's own bet; B is longer and cites a recited four-risk framework.
Fewer words, cuts the anxiety/insufficiency narration and gets to the point.
Guess comes before the answer is shown; A's wording about watching a second session is confusing.
Shorter and removes the filler line; blank-page contrast is plainly stated.
Cuts the low-value closing sentence, which also is not always true.
Removes passive 'nobody can hand you' phrasing less awkwardly; 'one run at a time' is concrete and matches the session frame.
The title states the point and the kicker line is no longer a redundant slogan after a title that already says it.
Cuts the parenthetical recap and the flywheel slogan.
Removes the clever trailing clause; shorter.
Cuts the closing aphorism that restates the point.
'Prompts' is the right word for what was run, matching the slide's references to prompts.
Shorter; B's extra wording adds little.
Cuts the forward hint to Module 4 and the course-self reference; plain statement of the practice.

Cuts the forward hint about Phase 3 and 4.
Adds concrete information on what the agent does, which makes the loop picturable.
'It often isn't. It's a draft' reads cleaner than 'just'; B's merged wording adds nothing, A keeps the slide's rhythm.
B's added sentence is about the course itself ('you are not learning them here'); cut it.

Cuts the redundant 'This is your side-quest lane' sentence.
Drops the redundant opener fragment, shorter and cleaner.

Concrete claim about recurring work having a shape; A's 'forest before trees' is a cliché metaphor.
Title states the point positively; A's title is a slightly abstract aphorism.

Concrete, picturable title; A's title is a longer abstract claim.

The closing line is a generic kicker after the point; cut it.
The header is accurate without a count, and the count does no memory work.
It names the action in fewer words, as in the author's own AE101 cut of this lead-in.
The closing line is a clever restatement; the figure and list already carry the point.
The permission line gives the student explicit leave to experiment, and the author keeps lines like that.
It is a concrete, shorter action for the student, which A's abstract wording is not.
A's orientation and 'names the pattern' lines are repeats and forward hints, which the author cuts.
